data.name: Bridge Constructor Stunts
data.detailed_description:
Bridge Constructor Stunts on Discord


Acerca do jogo

Stuntman and engineer in one? No problem with Bridge Constructor Stunts!
Build imposing ramps and loops to reach your goal in the diverse stages. But building structures alone isn't enough this time: you sit behind the wheel of the vehicles yourself and have to maneuver them skillfully to the goal. Collect stars, complete daredevil jumps, flips and spectacular stunts, leaving behind a trail of destruction across the entire level to beat the high score. But you can only do all that with perfectly constructed bridges and ramps.

Join the huge Let's Play community
To ensure none of your jumps are forgotten, you can save your runs as videos and GIFs, directly upload them to GIPHY and share them with your others (video export and GIF upload functions for Windows version only). Let the world be part of your most outrageous jumps!

Improved Construction Mode
Once again you have access to a variety of building materials with different properties. Numerous improvements make building even easier: simply click to convert a beam you have built into road, and vice-versa. Click and hold on a part of the construction and you now have the option to reposition your structures without having to build them from scratch.

Loose Screw!
We have hidden some hard-to-reach screws in some of the levels. Find and collect them, and you might be able to put these screws to good use in the future...

FEATURES:
  • The latest instalment in the internationally successful Bridge Constructor series!
  • Improved and simplified Construction Mode
  • Build ramps and drive vehicles across them yourself
  • Diverse level with different objectives: collect stars, score target, reach the goal…
  • Delivery vans and dump trucks with cargo that wreaks havoc when coming loose, but is also useful to help you collect items
  • Various building materials
  • Spectacular stunts and rampages of destruction
  • Achievements and rankings
  • Replay feature and video/GIF sharing: save your best bridge crossings and stunts and share them with your friends (video export and GIF upload functions for Window- s version only)
  • Controller-Support

reviews.review:
This game was played in its entirety on a MacBook Air M1 8gb ram 7c gpu running MacOS Sonoma. There were no bugs or crashes throughout my time with the game. All achievements unlocked at their appropriate times.

I won't mince words. This is not a good game. As many others have pointed out, this is a poor port of a mobile game. It shows, and many of its greatest weaknesses can be attributed to bad controls.

Let's start with the positives. It will be brief. The sound effects are pretty good. They are punchy, and you can really feel when your engine explodes. The graphics and level design are okay. They won't win any awards, but they aren't actively punching you in your stomach either.

On to the negatives, in general order from least to most offensive.

The music is pretty bad. It's only on a 20 second loop, so unless you have a Memento-style case of amnesia, this will get very old to your ears very quickly. I had to turn it off early on during my first play session.

The options are outrageous. There are two settings for music and sound effects. That is the sum total of the options. You want to run this windowed? Mobile devices can't run apps in windows so tough luck! ...they can?? Shaddap voices in my head!

The controls are either really bad (the driving) or outright criminal (the bridge building).

For driving, you have accelerate and brake. In case you are thinking I misspoke, no, there is no reverse. You will frequently have to create dummy ramps for yourself, just so you can give yourself some backwards momentum. It's a silly and stupid choice. Worse than no brake is how spinning works. You spin using the same keys as accelerate and brake (for clockwise and counter rotation respectively). You can't configure the keys (remember, options are for losers!), and the INSTANT one of your four tires leaves the planet (I did not name the planet; you'll see why later) your car shifts from vroom vroom mode to wheee spin me right round baby right round! mode. So, if your ramp is convex or sometimes even smooth, your vehicle will bounce up and immediately start spinning. And since you're accelerating, your engine will immediately pitch downwards, slam into the ramp, and explode right in your face.

The bridge controls are even worse, though they don't require much explanation. You have adding bridges or links of varying materials, moving said links, removing said links, and changing the links to roads. There are not many features here, but since it likely was accomplished with touch buttons on mobile devices, all of these have to be offloaded to the mouse. Be prepared to click and hold, and click and drag, and hold and click, and every other permutation you can think of!

The screen scrolling deserves special mention. All of the UI elements are on the edge of the screen. That's sensible! What's not is that the screen ALWAYS SCROLLS as soon as you approach an edge. So, any time you have to hit a button (how dare you!) you'll also have to reposition the screen afterwards. In a futuristic twist, you can actually control the camera with WASD, but you still can't stop the edge scrolling. So, if the button you need to click is on the right side of the screen, you can hold the A button, and the camera will move left and right with determination (but not sit still). Who wins here? No one. Who loses? Well, your fingers and your sanity, at a minimum.

On to the physics! This will be my favorite topic. Firstly, let's get this out of the way: the physics will change in every level you will play. I like to think that this is canon for the game, and you're being shipped off to different planets, planetoids, or even comets to complete your mission. Sometimes, you'll make a smooth ramp, and your vehicle will fall right off of it, as though its front winch was pre-attached to the core of the planet. Other times, you'll make THE SAME RAMP, and your vehicle will soar into the stratosphere, never to be seen again. I'm fairly convinced that the code actually makes a new vehicle for you at this point, identical to the previous one, as the first vehicle could not longer be found within the application.

Okay, so you have different physics in each level, but you could get used to that. Let's talk about the damage handling! Sometimes, you'll be traveling along a perfectly flat road. It will be the smoothest ride you've ever felt. Then, your panels fly off and your engine explodes in your face. What can you do? I like to call this Spontaneous Combustion of the Internal Combustion Engine. Classic Scot Ice am I right?

Other times, you'll go off a ramp really badly, smash engine first into a cliff, spin downwards hitting multiple steel beams and rocks, then land upside down in an abandoned firewords factory. You land so hard that several exploding barrels compete with each other to occupy the same coordinates in the space time continuum, which is inside of the vehicle's cab. Your PC's fans start to spin up just in PREPARATION of the explosion. When it happens, you close your eyes involuntarily, and you'll know you'll have some skin peeling off of your face later. The smoke clears and you haven't even scratched the paint.

TLDR: A bad mobile game port with something about Scot Ice in it. Thanks for coming to my STUNTS talk.
